extracted.intended_audience: Magma users writing and testing user intrinsics, package files, and using the Magma online help (beginner to intermediate programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for implementing, testing and packaging user intrinsics in the Magma system (error checking, signatures, spec files, imports), plus instructions for using the Magma online help/browser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures detect wrong argument category
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument types given in intrinsic signatures cause wrong argument categories to be detected immediately (e.g., intrinsic LowerToUpperCase(s::MonStgElt) will error if passed a non-string).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: calling LowerToUpperCase(4/7) produces a runtime error 'Bad argument types'. Use signatures to rely on automatic category/type checking for arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate argument element-type checking
rubrics_metrics.description: If an argument is an aggregate type (e.g. a sequence or set) the category/type of its elements should be tested as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: SequenceToString(q) has signature (<SeqEnum[MonStgElt]> q) and will error if q is not a sequence or if elements are not strings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use require-statement for general argument/parameter checks
rubrics_metrics.description: The require-statement tests any user-specified condition and, if false, stops execution and prints a message and the values of expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: require condition: expression list; If condition is false, Magma prints 'Runtime error in <intrinsic>: <message>' and displays the expression list (often a literal string).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use requirerange for integer range checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use requirerange v, L, U ; to verify an integer v lies in the closed interval [L .. U].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If L ≤ v ≤ U nothing happens; otherwise Magma prints an error message stating the problem (example: requirerange n, 0, 80; ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use requirege for lower-bound integer checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use requirege v, L; to verify integer v ≥ L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If v ≥ L nothing happens; otherwise Magma prints an error message stating the problem (example: requirege n, 1; ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include an expression list to give informative error output
rubrics_metrics.description: The expression list after require allows printing values (often a literal string) to help the user understand the runtime error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common pattern: require condition: "Descriptive error message"; or include more expressions like require #c eq 1: "Argument 1 (", c, ") should be a single string character";

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate string character sets with require
rubrics_metrics.description: When converting or manipulating strings, check that characters belong to the expected subset before proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: q := [ STC(c) : c in StringToSequence(s) ]; require q subset [STC("a")..STC("z")]: "String characters must be a, ..., z";

rubrics_metrics.name: Check divisors to avoid division by zero
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure any argument used as a divisor is checked (e.g., require b ne 0) to prevent division-by-zero runtime errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example recommendation: add require b ne 0: "Argument 2 cannot be 0"; in EuclideanAlgorithm after the comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameters in signatures are untyped — check them by hand
rubrics_metrics.description: Parameters (named/optional parameters) do not have types given in the signature, so their category/type must be validated explicitly inside the intrinsic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: require Category(Al) eq MonStgElt: "Parameter Al not a string"; require Category(n) eq RngIntElt: "Parameter n not an integer";

rubrics_metrics.name: Check parameter membership against allowed choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that a string parameter takes one of the permitted values before using it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: require Al in {"Trapezoid", "Simpson"}: "Parameter Al must be \"Trapezoid\" or \"Simpson\"";

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure integer-typed parameters and bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: For integer parameters, assert both the category and any required bounds (e.g., n is integer and n ≥ 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine checks: require Category(n) eq RngIntElt: "Parameter n not an integer"; requirege n, 1;

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on automatic coercion into RealField
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments that are elements of the real field must be supplied explicitly as such; integers and rationals will not be coerced automatically into the real field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example failure: calling Quadrature(Sin, 2, 5.3) produces 'Runtime error in Quadrature: Bad argument types' — supply 2.0 not 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spec file structure: filenames and directory trees
rubrics_metrics.description: A package spec file is a list of filenames in a tree format; items may be filenames or directory name followed by { items } to indicate contained files/directories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filenames are relative to the directory containing the spec file; separate filenames by whitespace and it is conventional (but not required) to put them on separate lines. Example shown with nested Grp { genlpck FP { ord1 ord2 } }.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation in spec files is optional but helpful
rubrics_metrics.description: Indentation is not essential for spec files, but useful to indicate tree structure to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The parser uses braces and whitespace; use indentation only for human readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach spec files with AttachSpec and detach with DetachSpec
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AttachSpec(F) to incorporate all package files named in spec file F into the current Magma session; use DetachSpec(F) to remove them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attaching a spec file has same effect as attaching all package files specified in it. If package files change, intrinsics update automatically; if the spec file itself changes you must detach and re-attach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use MAGMA_USER_SPEC to auto-attach spec files at startup
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the environment variable MAGMA_USER_SPEC to a colon-separated list of full pathnames of spec files to have them attached automatically at Magma startup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical usage in .cshrc: setenv MAGMA_USER_SPEC "$HOME/Magma/spec:/home/friend/specp"

rubrics_metrics.name: Make start-up spec packages frozen for performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages included in a start-up spec file should be made frozen to slightly decrease execution time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frozen packages do not auto-update when edited; bear this in mind during development/testing (unfrozen packages update automatically).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use import to share constants/identifiers among package files
rubrics_metrics.description: In a package file P, use import "filename" : identifier list; to bring identifiers from another package file into P with the same names and values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The named file must be included in the same spec file and attached when P is attached. If the source file changes later, automatic updating takes place in the context P.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer import over duplicating constants across packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Importing identifiers from a single definitions file is preferable to keeping separate copies of constants in each package file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: keep Z := IntegerRing(); R := RealField(); in mydefs and in other files use import "mydefs" : Z, R;

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrinsics update automatically when package files change (unless frozen)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a package file is edited and saved, attached intrinsics from that package are updated automatically in the session; if the package was frozen, this automatic update does not occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Attach("mypck1"); edit mypck1 and save; subsequent calls use the updated intrinsic without needing to re-attach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single online help requests (use ? )
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a single ? followed by a word (or ? alone) to request online help without entering the browser. If one node matches the word that node is shown; if several match they are listed with numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not end help requests with a semicolon. To view a listed node type ? followed by its number (e.g., ?6). Typing ? alone gives information about the help system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enter the online help browser with ??
rubrics_metrics.description: Type ?? from within Magma to enter the Magma Help Browser; the prompt becomes ??> and browser commands are used (not Magma statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Browser commands should not be followed by semicolons. Exit the browser with quit, exit or Ctrl-D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Browser navigation commands and node display
rubrics_metrics.description: Browser provides commands such as ls (list children), show (display node), where/pwd (current node), goto/cd (change node), up (parent), walk/back (traverse nodes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When show displays a node it prints PATH and KIND and lists subnodes and cross-references; 'show' by itself shows the current node.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding help nodes: find, delve, search
rubrics_metrics.description: Use find word to look for nodes referenced by the word (case-insensitive); use delve to search only at or below the current node; use search for exhaustive substring searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics are named as singular nouns (use 'polynomial' not 'polynomials'). Output of find/search is a numbered list of pathnames — view an entry by typing its number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of help nodes and their intended use
rubrics_metrics.description: Help nodes have kinds: Overview (O), Section (S), Intrinsic (I) and Example (E). Overview nodes are purpose-written for beginners and are concise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can restrict searches to node kinds using ofind/sfind/ifind/efind to focus on Overviews, Sections, Intrinsics or Examples respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references in help nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Nodes may include cross-references listed with special + numbers; these can be followed by +<number> at the browser prompt to view the referenced node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references often occur in SEE ALSO sections or inline (e.g., 'See [+1]'); type '+1' to follow the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tab completion in the browser
rubrics_metrics.description: On most systems pressing the tab key attempts to complete the current word against commands, references or pathnames; if multiple matches exist it expands to the common prefix and can list possibilities on a second press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If tab completion is not available, use search as the best substitute. If there are no possibilities the shell may beep.
